## devonthink
CRITICAL — Database package safety: DEVONthink databases are stored as packages (.dtBase2) or sparse images (.dtSparse, .dtArchive). Never modify, rename, move, or delete files inside a database package directly via the filesystem. All record and content operations must go through this MCP server or, as a fallback, via AppleScript. Direct filesystem manipulation will corrupt the database and cause irreversible data loss.

Batch operations: Use the uuids array parameter instead of sequential single-record calls for tag, update, move, trash, duplicate, replicate, and export operations. Batch mode is faster, reduces round trips, and returns a summary with succeeded/failed counts.

Avoiding duplicates: Use lookup_records (by name, URL, path, filename, or comment) before create_record to check whether a record already exists.

Content editing: Prefer update_record_content with mode append or insert over replace for large documents. Replace mode requires sending the entire new content and risks accidental data loss if the content is incomplete.

Group hierarchies: Use create_group_path to create nested group structures in a single call (like mkdir -p) rather than sequential create_record calls.

AI-powered tools: classify_record and find_similar_records use DEVONthink's built-in AI algorithms and proprietary training data — they provide organizational suggestions that complement, not duplicate, your own capabilities.

Record enrichment: resolve_doi_metadata and resolve_book_metadata can enrich existing records with bibliographic metadata by passing the record's uuid — there is no need to create a new record.

AI exclusion: Records marked as excluded from AI access (excludeFromChat) are protected in two ways. (1) Input protection: any tool that receives such a record's UUID as an argument refuses to operate on it and returns an error. (2) Output protection: result lists from tools like search_records, classify_record, find_similar_records, get_record_children, get_record_duplicates, and the link traversal tools are filt… [truncated]

content.text: She's currently filed under `client/` with "Direction: To client" — but a government payments contact isn't really a client relationship. Before I make changes: what would you like the new category folder to be called (e.g. `contacts/`, `external/`, `vendors/`)? And should its email-history "Direction" labels read "To contact" / "From contact" (or similar), matching the pattern used for clients/colleagues/friends?
Are conversations like this worth tracking?

Depends on why you're keeping the CRM at all — if it's for relationship management (remembering context before a call, tracking rapport), a one-off payments contact like Josée probably isn't worth full tracking; if it's more of an email-log/reference tool (recall what was said, when), then yes, low-touch admin contacts are exactly what benefits from a lightweight record since you won't remember the details otherwise.

My lean: keep a minimal record (name, email, one-line purpose) but skip the full "## Mark's Email History" thread-by-thread treatment reserved for clients/friends/colleagues — that section is expensive to maintain and adds little value for a contact you interact with rarely. Want me to set up a lightweight `other/` (or similar) category with a stripped-down format, or would you rather just drop occasional contacts like her entirely and let `gmail-sync` skip them?
Add Josee to the ignore list and delete her entry.

content.text:
Works — no more manual `op` prefix needed, and `--` passthrough args flow through correctly.

Both Gmail scripts now self-invoke 1Password:

```json
"gmail-login": "env \"$(op environment read ko66mhzn54ipyinybf2ftfci3q)\" tsx src/gmail-login.ts",
"gmail-sync":  "env \"$(op environment read ko66mhzn54ipyinybf2ftfci3q)\" tsx src/gmail-sync.ts",
```

So `npm run gmail-sync` (and `npm run gmail-sync -- <files>`) and `npm run gmail-login` now just work — the `env "$(op environment read …)"` resolves `GMAIL_OAUTH_SECRET` at run time and never persists it.

One thing worth flagging: I hardcoded the environment ID `ko66mhzn54ipyinybf2ftfci3q` into the checked-in `package.json`, whereas the rest of the repo (`gmail-auth.ts`, `gmail-sync.ts`, `docs/PRD-gmail-sync.md`) deliberately uses a `<item-id>` placeholder. The ID itself isn't a secret — it's useless without an authenticated 1Password session — but if you'd prefer to keep it out of version control I can instead read it from an env var (e.g. `$OP_GMAIL_ENV_ID`) that you set in your shell profile. Want me to switch to that, and/or update the stale `<item-id>` references in the docs/comments to match?
